purpose: Lightweight education ontology for Ask Theo so compound-name questions get useful research-literacy answers before the deeper source brain is fully populated.
answerRules: Use this map for plain-English identification, category, mechanism themes, COA/label checks, and uncertainty notes.
Do not convert any entry into medical advice, dosing guidance, route guidance, protocol instructions, cycles, stacks, or treatment claims.
If the user asks what to take, how much to take, how to use it, how to inject it, or how to run a stack/cycle, use the safety boundary instead.

categories.name: mitochondrial-energy
categories.description: Compounds commonly discussed around mitochondrial signaling, redox biology, exercise response, cellular energy, and metabolic research.

items.name: MOTS-c
aliases: mitochondrial open reading frame of the 12S rRNA-c
items.explain: MOTS-c is a 16-amino-acid mitochondrial-derived peptide studied as a signaling molecule between mitochondria and the nucleus, especially in metabolism and stress-response research.

items.name: SS-31
items.explain: SS-31, also called elamipretide, is studied for mitochondrial membrane and cardiolipin-related biology, not as a generic supplement.

items.name: Humanin
items.explain: Humanin is a mitochondrial-derived peptide discussed in cell-stress, aging, and neurobiology research.

items.name: NAD+
items.explain: NAD+ is a core cellular cofactor involved in redox reactions and signaling pathways tied to energy metabolism, DNA repair, and aging biology.

items.name: NMN
items.explain: NMN is a precursor in the NAD+ salvage pathway and is usually discussed as part of NAD+ biology rather than as a standalone miracle compound.

items.name: NR
items.explain: Nicotinamide riboside is another NAD+ precursor studied for how it may influence NAD+ availability and related cellular pathways.

items.name: CoQ10
items.explain: CoQ10 is a naturally occurring mitochondrial cofactor involved in electron transport and antioxidant chemistry.

items.name: PQQ
items.explain: PQQ is discussed as a redox-active nutrient-like compound, often around mitochondrial biogenesis claims that need careful source checking.

categories.name: metabolic-exercise-mimetic
categories.description: Research compounds discussed around exercise-response pathways, muscle metabolism, glucose/lipid biology, and body-composition models.

items.name: SLU-PP-332
items.explain: SLU-PP-332 is a synthetic research compound studied as an estrogen-related receptor agonist, often framed as an exercise-mimetic pathway probe in metabolic research.

items.name: SLU-PP-915
items.explain: SLU-PP-915 is a related ERR-agonist research compound discussed in newer exercise-capacity and metabolic-pathway studies.

items.name: AICAR
items.explain: AICAR is a research compound used to probe AMPK-related energy-sensing biology.

items.name: GW501516
items.explain: GW501516, often called Cardarine online, is a PPAR-delta agonist research compound with major safety and compliance baggage; Theo should keep it strictly educational.

items.name: 5-Amino-1MQ
items.explain: 5-Amino-1MQ is discussed as an NNMT-related research compound in metabolic and adipocyte biology contexts.

items.name: Tesofensine
items.explain: Tesofensine is a drug candidate studied in metabolic and appetite-related clinical contexts, so Theo should treat it differently from research peptides.

categories.name: glp-gip-amylin
categories.description: Incretin and satiety-pathway compounds that require especially careful educational-only framing.

items.name: Semaglutide
items.explain: Semaglutide is a GLP-1 receptor agonist with prescription-drug context; Theo can explain mechanism and label/COA terms, not use guidance.

items.name: Tirzepatide
items.explain: Tirzepatide is a dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist with prescription-drug context; education should focus on mechanism and terminology.

items.name: Retatrutide
items.explain: Retatrutide is discussed as a multi-receptor incretin-pathway compound in clinical research, not as a casual supplement.

items.name: Cagrilintide
items.explain: Cagrilintide is an amylin-pathway compound studied in satiety and metabolic clinical contexts.

items.name: Mazdutide
items.explain: Mazdutide is a GLP-1/glucagon receptor agonist discussed in metabolic research and clinical-trial contexts.

categories.name: growth-repair
categories.description: Peptides commonly discussed around tissue repair, growth-hormone axis research, sleep/recovery claims, and inflammation models.

items.name: BPC-157
items.explain: BPC-157 is a synthetic peptide fragment discussed heavily online for repair biology, but much of the evidence landscape is preclinical and claim-heavy.

items.name: TB-500
items.explain: TB-500 is commonly discussed as a thymosin beta-4-related research peptide around cell migration and tissue-remodeling models.

items.name: Thymosin alpha-1
items.explain: Thymosin alpha-1 is an immune-modulating peptide with a different evidence and regulatory context than many online research peptides.

items.name: CJC-1295
items.explain: CJC-1295 is a GHRH analog discussed around growth-hormone-axis research; Theo should avoid protocol or stack advice.

items.name: Ipamorelin
items.type: growth hormone secretagogue receptor agonist peptide
items.explain: Ipamorelin is a GHSR-related peptide discussed around growth-hormone-axis signaling and recovery claims.

items.name: Sermorelin
items.explain: Sermorelin is a GHRH analog with clinical and research contexts around pituitary growth-hormone signaling.

items.name: Tesamorelin
items.explain: Tesamorelin is a GHRH analog with prescription/clinical context, so Theo should explain it with extra care.

items.name: GHK-Cu
items.explain: GHK-Cu is a copper-binding tripeptide often discussed around skin, matrix remodeling, and cosmetic research.

categories.name: immune-thymic
categories.description: Compounds commonly discussed around immune signaling, thymic peptides, inflammation, and immune education.

items.name: Thymulin
items.explain: Thymulin is a thymic peptide hormone discussed in immune-signaling and inflammation research.

items.name: LL-37
items.explain: LL-37 is an antimicrobial peptide involved in innate immune signaling and inflammation biology.

items.name: Epitalon
items.explain: Epitalon is a tetrapeptide discussed around aging and telomerase claims; Theo should separate documented evidence from online extrapolation.

categories.name: cognitive-neuro
categories.description: Peptides and nootropic-like compounds discussed around cognition, neuroplasticity, stress, sleep, and neural signaling.

items.name: Semax
items.explain: Semax is an ACTH-derived peptide analog discussed in neurobiology and cognition contexts, with region-specific drug history.

items.name: Selank
items.explain: Selank is a tuftsin-derived peptide analog discussed around stress and neuropeptide signaling, with region-specific drug history.

items.name: Dihexa
items.explain: Dihexa is a high-uncertainty research compound discussed around synaptogenesis and neuroplasticity claims; Theo should be careful not to overstate it.

items.name: Noopept
items.explain: Noopept is a nootropic-like peptide analog discussed around cognition claims and neurotrophic signaling.

items.name: DSIP
items.explain: DSIP is a sleep-related peptide with mixed and historically messy evidence, so Theo should frame it cautiously.

categories.name: hormone-related
categories.description: Peptides and compounds tied to melanocortin, reproductive, or endocrine signaling; these need cautious educational framing.

items.name: PT-141
items.explain: PT-141, also known as bremelanotide, is a melanocortin receptor agonist with prescription-drug context.

items.name: Melanotan II
items.explain: Melanotan II is a melanocortin receptor agonist peptide discussed around pigmentation and other melanocortin effects, with substantial safety concerns.

items.name: Kisspeptin
items.explain: Kisspeptin is a reproductive-axis signaling peptide involved in GnRH-related endocrine biology.

items.name: HCG
items.explain: HCG is a glycoprotein hormone with fertility and endocrine clinical contexts, not a casual supplement.

categories.name: longevity-senolytic-supplement
categories.description: Common supplement-like or longevity-adjacent compounds that Theo should know at a literacy level.

items.name: Fisetin
items.explain: Fisetin is a flavonoid discussed around senolytic and inflammation-related research, with many claims still preclinical.

items.name: Quercetin
items.explain: Quercetin is a flavonoid commonly discussed in polyphenol, inflammation, and senolytic-stack contexts.

items.name: Spermidine
items.explain: Spermidine is a polyamine studied around autophagy and cellular aging biology.

items.name: Taurine
items.explain: Taurine is an amino sulfonic acid involved in several physiological processes and discussed in aging and stress-biology research.

items.name: Urolithin A
items.explain: Urolithin A is a metabolite discussed around mitophagy, muscle, and aging research.

items.name: Resveratrol
items.explain: Resveratrol is a polyphenol famous for sirtuin and longevity claims, but Theo should clearly separate mechanism hype from human evidence.

items.name: Rapamycin
items.explain: Rapamycin, also called sirolimus, is an mTOR inhibitor drug discussed in longevity research and clinical medicine; it needs careful evidence and risk framing.

items.name: Metformin
items.explain: Metformin is a prescription metabolic drug often discussed in longevity circles; Theo can explain mechanisms and studies, not advise use.
